svg.title: Immersion objectives
svg.desc: Rays leave a specimen on a cover glass at the same angle and refract into the medium between the cover glass and the objective. In air (a) the ray bends far from the axis and misses the objective; in water (b), n = 1.33, it bends less; in oil (c), n = 1.51, almost not at all, so more rays enter the objective. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Immersion changes refraction and numerical aperture
Same objective aperture and cover-glass ray in all three cases
NA = n sin 45°. Cover glass n = 1.52; its ray angle is 35°. Snell’s law sets each emerging angle;
this example collects the water and oil rays.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
